metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully starred all 2 emails in Bills folder using Ctrl+A to select all, then right-click > Mark > Add Star.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select all emails, use right-click Mark submenu for both starring and tagging (Tags > Important follows same menu path).
metadata.explanation: Chains the original starring task with an Important tag ($label1) objective. Evaluator reads Bills mbox checking (1) X-Mozilla-Status bit 0x0004 for starred, (2) X-Mozilla-Keys header contains '$label1' for Important tag. Each sub-goal contributes 0.5 to the score.

scoring_breakdown.all_starred: 0.5 - All Bills emails have X-Mozilla-Status flagged bit (0x0004) set
scoring_breakdown.all_important: 0.5 - All Bills emails have '$label1' in X-Mozilla-Keys header

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the Bills mbox file from the expected Thunderbird profile path, which is deterministic for this snapshot.
mbox splitting via '^From - ' regex is correct for Thunderbird Local Folders format, which uses 'From - [timestamp]' as the separator.
X-Mozilla-Status bit 0x0004 is the correct Thunderbird flag for 'starred' (marked) status; deleted messages (0x0008) are correctly filtered out.
$label1 in X-Mozilla-Keys is the correct Thunderbird internal identifier for the 'Important' tag, accurately mapping the instruction's 'tag as Important' requirement.
Postconfig kills Thunderbird before reading mbox, ensuring data is flushed to disk before evaluation.
Metric awards 0.5 partial credit per sub-goal (starred + important), correctly handles empty mailbox (returns 0.0), and handles error responses.
The evaluator covers ALL requirements of the instruction: both starring and tagging as Important are independently verified.
Initial state (no stars, no Important tag) will fail both checks, providing negative-control resistance.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The metric function ignores the 'expected' parameter entirely and hardcodes the pass condition in the getter's boolean fields. This is functionally correct but slightly unconventional; documenting this design choice would improve clarity.
